items.title: Google Makes MCP the Only Front Door for AI Agents in Workspace
items.summary: Google's eight Workspace MCP servers (Gmail, Calendar, Drive, Docs, Sheets, Slides, Chat, Tasks) are now generally available alongside an official Workspace CLI. The new Workspace AI Tools Addendum, effective Feb 1 2027, requires AI agents and similar access tools to reach Workspace data through those MCP servers or the CLI instead of calling REST APIs directly. REST-only agents will be capped at Standard Tier quotas no matter which tier the project selects, and the internal-use exception does not apply to MCP quotas. Standard Tier allows 5,000 requests per day per project per product with no billing account; Scaled Tier billing starts Apr 1 2027, when the free MCP allowance disappears for Gmail, Calendar and Drive and usage is charged from the first successful request. Admins get agent-specific OAuth identity, confirmation prompts for sensitive actions, existing DLP rules, audit logs, and a quota dashboard; rollout completes within two weeks.
items.impact: MCP shifts from an optional integration to a governed platform boundary with a hard migration deadline. Agents built on raw Workspace REST APIs face throttling or a cost jump, and this is a likely template for other SaaS vendors deciding how to expose data to agents.

items.title: Uber Evals 1 Million+ Agent Skill Invocations a Month Across 5,000 Skills
items.summary: Uber published its operating model for agent skills: a shared Git-backed marketplace grew from one skill in Oct 2025 to more than 5,000 (5,300+ in the post's chart), with over one million skill invocations in a single month. One SKILL.md format runs in Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Cursor and Uber's hosted agents; an aifx CLI handles identity, distribution and MCP connections through six merged configuration layers. The marketplace has three tiers: Domain (one peer review plus CI), Core (platform-team review), and about 100 Always-on skills enabled for everyone. Authors write a spec.md first and Skill Workshop compiles the skill and its tests from it. Eval suites mix roughly 5% golden cases, 80% real prompts graded on trajectory and 15% author cases; real prompts are replayed with and without a skill and judged blind. For one warehouse-query skill, going without it meant 13% more tool calls, six times the tool errors and 31% longer runtime, and the skilled answer won 87% of comparisons. Uber argues 70-90% eval pass rates are more informative than 100% because LLM judges are noisy. Telemetry records skill and version but no prompt text or file contents.
items.impact: This is the first detailed public account of skills as managed software: versioned, owned, tested, measured and retired at fleet scale. It pushes agent quality from prompt craft toward ordinary engineering discipline, and a portable skill format makes accumulated workflow knowledge an asset that survives harness changes. All figures are Uber's own telemetry and ablations.

items.title: Pydantic Ships Pax: a Terminal Coding Agent Where Everything Is a Plugin
items.summary: Pydantic released pydantic-ai-pax, a command-line coding agent built on its own Harness SDK. Every capability is a plugin toggled with /plugins: the coder, sandbox, MCP support and Logfire observability are all optional. Switch off the coder plugin and Pax becomes a chat client with no file or shell tools; asked appropriately, it can even write a new plugin for itself. The --agent flag loads any Pydantic AI Agent from the repository with its own model, tools and instructions and skips the default plugins, so the same Agent object can be debugged in a real terminal and then deployed unchanged as a service. Pydantic also said Harness reaches 1.0 in about a month and will follow Pydantic AI's versioning policy; Harness has accumulated 100+ pluggable capabilities since June, including persistent execution, more than ten sandboxes and workspaces, model fallback, subagents and context management.
items.impact: Pax collapses the debug-to-deploy gap: the agent you exercise locally is the artifact you ship. Plugin composition also makes capability boundaries explicit, letting teams remove file and shell access instead of relying on prompt-level restrictions. It points toward coding agents becoming configurable runtimes rather than fixed products. Sourced from a single report with no benchmarks published yet.

items.title: AGIBOT Reports 30,000 Robot Agents Built on Its LinkSoul Platform
items.summary: AGIBOT released first-year numbers for LinkSoul, the robot-agent development platform at the center of its AIMA embodied-AI ecosystem and YuanSheng plan: over 20,000 users, more than 30,000 created robot agents and over 70,000 pieces of platform content. Users describe tasks in natural language, assemble knowledge bases and skill modules, orchestrate workflows, and debug behavior in a 3D simulation environment instead of repeatedly trialing on hardware. SDK, MCP and Skill interfaces connect agents to external tools and existing business systems. Reported use cases include park interaction, venue guidance, reception and inspection tours; validated agents, skill packs and workflows are retained as reusable assets. AGIBOT has committed at least 2 billion yuan over five years to the ecosystem. The company itself flags open problems: standardized evaluation of community-created agents, real-machine reliability and a repeatable commercial loop.
items.impact: This targets the real scaling bottleneck in embodied AI, which is application development cost rather than robot hardware. Letting domain staff configure and iterate on robots instead of requiring an algorithm team per scenario could change deployment economics if the reusable skill library actually compounds. The figures are company-reported, and agent count is not the same as production deployments.

items.title: NIO Unveils NWM 3.0 World Model With 5x Training Efficiency and a December Rollout
items.summary: At NIO IN 2026 in Guangzhou, NIO launched NIO WorldModel 3.0 for intelligent driving. Tubelet-based 4D spatiotemporal compression cuts onboard attention compute by 36 times; coordinated algorithm, chip and chassis optimization reduces chassis control latency by 78% and overall vehicle control latency by 54%. A dual closed-loop reinforcement-learning framework, one loop in observation space and one in latent space, delivers five times the training efficiency of the previous generation, and a new reward model supports more dynamic real-world evaluation. NIO reports 40% fewer driver interventions and about 60% higher user reassurance. NWM 3.0 goes to Banyan, Cedar, Cedar S and Coconut+ users from December after regulatory filing and clearance. NIO also launched NOMI Intelligence 4.0 with a vehicle-native agent framework, and said it has deployed 7,500+ internal AI agents with 2.9 million+ executions.
items.impact: This is a rare physical-AI result with quantified latency gains and a concrete ship date, moving world models from benchmark demos toward fleet deployment. For real-time control, cutting inference and actuation latency matters more than another benchmark point. All improvements are NIO's own measurements, the intervention figure has no independent validation, and the rollout depends on regulatory clearance.
